title: The JSE: Africa's $1.5 Trillion Stock Market and Its Shrinking List | The Six, Ep. 3
lede: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange is worth more than thirteen times Nigeria's exchange, the next largest in Africa, yet it lists fewer companies every year. By one count, thirteen companies are leaving in 2026 and two have joined. This episode explains where the value comes from, why companies delist, and what the JSE and its rivals are doing about it.
keyPoints: Companies listed on the JSE were worth about US$1.55 trillion in August 2026, more than 13 times Nigeria's exchange (World Federation of Exchanges).
About 68% of that value, roughly R16 trillion of R24.7 trillion, sits in 59 inward listings whose main listing is elsewhere (JSE, June 2026).
257 companies were listed in August 2026, down 6.9% in a year. A UCT study counts 514 delistings since 1989 and a 7.8% annual delisting rate in 1993–2015, against 4.1% globally.
AmaranthCX counts 195 JSE delistings and 71 new listings since 2017; 2026's only two arrivals were secondary listings (Aimia and Canal+).

The JSE's simplified Listings Requirements took effect in January and February 2026, cutting the rulebook by more than half. Omnia's shareholders vote on a R21.8 billion offer from Solar Industries on Nov. 5.
